system_prompt: You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.
a1_answer:
DESIGN/INDICATOR: Mass flow rate deviation from the hydraulic model prediction, calculated using a Kalman filter-based real-time hydraulic model incorporating pressure and flow measurements at both ends of the pipeline segment.

THRESHOLD: A sustained mass flow imbalance of 0.3% of nominal flow for 6 consecutive measurement periods (30 minutes total), with at least 3 points exceeding 0.25% in that window.

FALSIFICATION TEST: Apply the algorithm to 12 months of historical operational data from 10 identical pipeline segments with confirmed leak-free operation. Count any segment that triggers the alarm more than once in this period. If any segment exceeds this false alarm rate, the predictor is falsified and must be redesigned.

USER CONSTRAINT: Must use only existing pressure and flow transmitters at 5-minute intervals
RATIONALE: Directly addresses the operational data availability constraint.

USER CONSTRAINT: Must detect a leak of 0.5% of nominal flow within 48 hours
RATIONALE: Establishes the minimum detection sensitivity and timeliness requirement.

USER CONSTRAINT: Not raise more than 1 false alarm per month per 10 km of pipe
RATIONALE: Defines the acceptable false positive rate for operational deployment.

CALCULATED: 0.3% threshold for 6 consecutive periods
RATIONALE: Balances detection sensitivity with false alarm rate by requiring sustained deviation rather than transient fluctuations.

ASSUMPTION: Pipeline segments are approximately 10 km in length
RATIONALE: Provides a practical segment length for monitoring and matches the false alarm rate constraint specification.

ASSUMPTION: Historical data quality is sufficient for baseline hydraulic model calibration
RATIONALE: Necessary for the Kalman filter-based approach to establish normal operating conditions.

CALCULATED: 30-minute detection window (6×5-minute intervals)
RATIONALE: Provides sufficient time to confirm a persistent imbalance while maintaining the 48-hour detection requirement for small leaks.
